summary: A proposal by Alex McKenzie for a software consulting service for network users. Users with real problems lacked help, because the Resources Notebook updated slowly and technical liaisons were often busy systems programmers. The note describes a service to fill that gap.

eli5.summary: A helpdesk idea so beginners can ask a patient person for help.

subtitle: A help desk for people learning to use the early network

tldr.problem: Users with real problems to solve lacked good software support; the Resources Notebook updated too slowly, and Technical Liaisons were often busy systems programmers working odd hours.
tldr.mechanism: BBN hired Nancy Neigus as a software consultant with expertise in network systems and subsystems. She would be available weekdays 9 AM to 5 PM Eastern Time to help users with their network problems.
tldr.outcome: The software consulting service became a channel for users to get patient help with network issues, and it also could help debug protocol implementations and dispatch problems to relevant systems.

facts.label: Available hours
facts.value: 9 AM to 5 PM Eastern Time, weekdays

today: This was the beginning of professional network support and user assistance services. The concept of a dedicated software consultant for network users was novel in 1972, and it established a model for user support that would become standard in later networking organizations.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content: As network use grew, it became clear that users with real problems needed software assistance and consulting services. Two existing mechanisms had fallen short: the Resources Notebook was too slow to update, and Technical Liaisons were usually systems programmers who worked odd hours and were impatient with naive users' questions.
sections.eli5: When people wanted help using the network, the documentation was out of date and the expert programmers were too busy or grumpy.

sections.title: The Software Consultant
sections.content: To solve this problem, BBN hired Nancy Neigus as a software consultant for the Network Control Center. Nancy had extensive experience with network systems and subsystems, having spent months learning about them over the network. This consulting service was experimental in nature, meaning its scope and continued existence would depend on how useful it proved to the user community.
sections.eli5: BBN hired Nancy, a friendly person who knows how networks work, to help users figure out their problems.

sections.title: What Nancy Could Help With
sections.content: The primary goal was for Nancy to provide assistance in using existing network resources. The service also could help with checkout of protocol implementations and resolution of conflicts between systems. In some cases, if network operation required changes to host software, Nancy and BBN could act as a repository and dispatch point for reported problems.
sections.eli5: Nancy can help you use the network, test new protocols, and report bugs to the right place.

sections.title: How to Reach Nancy
sections.content: Nancy was available on weekdays between 9 AM and 5 PM Eastern Time. Users could reach her by phone through the Network Control Center at (617) 611-0100 (collect calls accepted) or leave messages online at the NIC for 'NJN'. TIP users could also use the Gripe service. The NCC had round-the-clock operator coverage and would take messages for Nancy at other times.
sections.eli5: You can call or leave a message to reach Nancy during business hours, and other times someone will take a message for her.
